notes: Account background: Loopline is a mid-market analytics SaaS (B2B) offering KPI search + contextual recommendations embedded inside customer dashboards.
Primary problem: current search is keyword-based, poor recall; want semantic search over metrics + docs for in-app help and discovery.
Current infra: Postgres + pgvector for 2M vectors, nightly ETL generates ~500k new vectors/month. Evaluating move to specialized vector layer for scale.
POC goals: validate embeddings throughput (ingest 500k/day), query latency at scale (target 95p < 120ms for 300 qps), and integration with existing Postgres-backed metadata.
Throughput requirements: peak query load ~300 qps (dashboard spikes), background batch job ingest ~50-200k vectors/hour during processing windows.
Quality/model preferences: open to OpenAI-style embeddings or open models; priority is consistency and deterministic embeddings across runs. Want model pinning for reproducibility.
Routing/fallback needs: prefer Hosted API for initial rollout; plan to shift to Dedicated for predictable throughput and cost controls once ARR ~>$100k.
Security/compliance: require SSO (SAML), audit logging for vector changes, KMS-managed keys, and EU data residency for some customers.
Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to trade some latency for 30% lower cost; team interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization.
Technical notes from POC: Hosted API handled single-shot ingest bursts ~2k vectors/sec for 60s in early tests; end-to-end ingest pipeline issues due to their ETL single-threaded uploader.
POC findings (prelim): query P95 on Hosted with caching warmed ~85ms at 50 qps; at 200 qps P95 increased to ~220ms — motivates Dedicated sizing + autoscale policies.
Quoted from CTO: 'We need predictable tail latency during end-of-month reporting spikes; intermittent 200+ ms responses are unacceptable for the product team.'
Integration asks: connector for Postgres metadata, sample code for batch bulk-indexing, and an example of prefix/KV cache for frequently accessed vectors.
Operational asks: cold-start warmup strategy, recommended autoscale thresholds, and a breakdown of per-token vs per-embedding cost for hybrid workloads.
Next steps agreed: run full-scale ingest simulation (8M vectors) in a Dedicated trial environment; Redwood to provide a temporary Dedicated sizing quote and runbook for integration.
Blockers called out by security: need SOC2 attestation + network diagram for VPC peering; finance needs 3 pricing scenarios (hosted, reserved Dedicated, burst-only Dedicated).
Notes on competitors: customer has done initial evals with Pinecone (good ops), Elastic (cost for scale), Weaviate (open stack). They view Redwood as attractive for unified host->dedicated path.
Sales tactica: emphasize Redwood Optimize (batch suggestions), rolling upgrade/rollout tooling, and migration playbook from Hosted -> Dedicated.
Misc: Jira ticket RDW-2109 opened for a request to add a pgvector import example; awaiting SE response.
